title: 讲座：实验报告写作（新题型优化版所供原文）

待核: 讲座列表1—5为解析排版编号，当前未写额外口述数字，须据ASR核是否实际朗读数字。

程序仅绑定ASR候选，不等于源文或音轨已通过人工核验；须复核本年对齐报告的全部差异及未覆盖ASR段。
仍有5个原文词缺少ASR对应；涉及句号[4, 19, 37, 48, 49]，严禁按比例补时。

sentences.en: Good morning, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家早上好。

sentences.en: Today we’ll discuss some preliminaries concerning how to write experimental reports.
sentences.zh: 今天我们来讨论撰写实验报告前需要了解的一些基本事项。

sentences.en: When you first signed up for a course in university, like a psychology course, chances are that you didn’t really expect what was coming in your study; particularly, the course emphasis on methodology and statistics.
sentences.zh: 刚在大学选修一门课，比如心理学时，你很可能并没有真正预料到将要学习什么，尤其没有想到课程会强调研究方法和统计学。

sentences.en: For a few of you, this may have come as a pleasant surprise, provided that you have already known something about the course.
sentences.zh: 如果你事先对这门课已有所了解，那么对你们当中的少数人来说，这可能是个惊喜。

sentences.en: For most, however, I dare say, it will undoubtedly have been a shock to the system.
sentences.zh: 不过，对大多数人来说，我想这无疑会是一次强烈的冲击。

w.m: phr.令人难以适应的强烈冲击

sentences.en: No doubt in other parts of your course study, you will read books and journals, examining, critically, models and theories, assumptions and hypotheses put forward by scholars and specialists.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，在课程学习的其他部分，你们会阅读书籍和期刊，批判性地考察学者和专家提出的模型、理论、假设和假说。

sentences.en: My task today is to help you understand some of the important features of experimental reports, because you will have to write up some kind of report of this nature if your course gives prominence to practical work, especially experimenting.
sentences.zh: 我今天的任务是帮助你们了解实验报告的一些重要特点，因为如果课程重视实践，尤其是实验，你们就必须撰写这类报告。

sentences.en: Then what is an experimental report?
sentences.zh: 那么，什么是实验报告呢？

sentences.en: All a report is, really, is the place in which you tell the story of your study, like what you did, why you did it, what you found out in the process, and so on.
sentences.zh: 说到底，报告就是一个讲述研究经过的载体，例如你做了什么、为什么这样做、在过程中发现了什么，等等。

sentences.en: In doing this, you are more like an ancient storyteller, whose stories were structured in accordance with widely recognized and long-established conventions, than a modern novelist who is free to dictate form as well as content.
sentences.zh: 写报告时，你更像古代的说书人，要按照公认且历史悠久的惯例来组织故事，而不像可以自由决定形式与内容的现代小说家。

sentences.en: Moreover, like the storyteller of old, although you will invariably be telling your story to someone who knows quite a bit about it already, you are expected to present it as if it had never been heard before.
sentences.zh: 而且，像旧时的说书人一样，尽管听众往往已经很了解你的故事，你仍然要把它当作一个从未被听过的故事来讲。

sentences.en: This means that you will need to spell out the details and assume little knowledge of the area on the part of your audience.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你要把细节交代清楚，并假定读者对这个领域知之甚少。

sentences.en: Then, perhaps, you may ask, what is the nature of the conventions governing the report?
sentences.zh: 接下来，你也许会问，报告所遵循的惯例究竟是什么样的？

sentences.en: A clue, I think, can be found in its basic structure.
sentences.zh: 我认为，可以从报告的基本结构中找到线索。

sentences.en: A highly structured and disciplined report is written in sections, and these sections, by and large, follow an established sequence.
sentences.zh: 一份结构严谨、合乎规范的报告是分节写成的，而这些章节大体上遵循既定的顺序。

sentences.en: What this means is that, in the telling, your story is to be cut up into chunks: different parts of the story are to appear in different places in the report.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，在叙述时，你要把研究经过分成若干部分，让不同内容出现在报告的不同位置。

sentences.en: What you did and why you did it appear in the section called INTRODUCTION.
sentences.zh: 你做了什么以及为什么这样做，应写在“引言”部分。

sentences.en: How you did it is in the METHOD section.
sentences.zh: 你是怎样做的，应写在“方法”部分。

sentences.en: And what you found out is in the RESULT section.
sentences.zh: 而你发现了什么，应写在“结果”部分。

sentences.en: And, finally, what you think it shows appears in the DISCUSSION part.
sentences.zh: 最后，你认为这些结果说明了什么，应写在“讨论”部分。

sentences.en: As you can see, the report, therefore, is a formal document composed of a series of sections in which specific information is expected to appear.
sentences.zh: 因此，正如你所见，报告是一份正式文档，由一系列章节组成，每节都应呈现特定的信息。

sentences.en: We will discuss the precise conventions governing each section as we go along.
sentences.zh: 随着讲解的推进，我们会讨论各节具体应遵循的规范。

sentences.en: For example, what are the subsections in the METHOD?
sentences.zh: 例如，“方法”部分包含哪些小节？

sentences.en: But today, I will introduce to you certain general rules straight away.
sentences.zh: 不过，今天我会先直接介绍几条基本规则。

sentences.en: The first of these concerns the person to whom you should address your report, whom I shall call “your reader”.
sentences.zh: 第一条涉及报告的写作对象，我将其称为“你的读者”。

sentences.en: A very common mistake, especially early on, is to assume that your reader is the person who will be marking the report.
sentences.zh: 一个很常见的错误，尤其在初学时，就是以为读者是给报告评分的人。

sentences.en: In reality, however, the marker will be assessing your report on behalf of someone else—an idealized, hypothetical person who is intelligent but unknowledgeable about your study and the area in which it took place.
sentences.zh: 然而，实际上，评分人是在代另一个人评估报告：这是一个理想化、假想的读者，虽然聪明，却不了解你的研究及其所属领域。

sentences.en: Your marker will, therefore, be checking to see that you have written your report with this sort of reader in mind.
sentences.zh: 所以，评分人会检查你写报告时是否考虑到了这种读者。

w.h: with this sort of reader in mind

sentences.en: So you need to make sure that you have introduced the reader to the area relevant to your study.
sentences.zh: 因此，你要确保已经向读者介绍了与你的研究相关的领域。

sentences.en: Provided the reader with the background necessary to understand what you did and why you did it.
sentences.zh: 向读者提供必要的背景，使其理解你做了什么以及为什么这样做。

sentences.en: Spelt out and developed your arguments clearly.
sentences.zh: 清楚地阐明并展开你的论点。

sentences.en: Defined technical terms.
sentences.zh: 给专业术语下定义。

sentences.en: And provided precise details of the way in which you went about collecting and analyzing the data that you obtained.
sentences.zh: 并准确、详细地交代你是怎样收集和分析所获数据的。

sentences.en: In short, you should write for someone who knows little about your area of study, taking little for granted about your reader’s knowledge of your area of study.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，你应当为不了解研究领域的人写作，不要想当然地认为读者具备相关知识。

sentences.en: So when in doubt, spell it out.
sentences.zh: 所以，有疑问时就把它讲清楚。

sentences.en: This is my advice to you.
sentences.zh: 这就是我给你们的建议。

sentences.en: If you find this difficult to do, then a useful approach is to write the report as if it would be read by someone you know who is intelligent but unknowledgeable about your subject.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得这很难做到，一个有用的办法是：写报告时，想象读者是你认识的某个人，虽聪明，却不了解你的研究课题。

sentences.en: A friend of yours, say.
sentences.zh: 比如，你的一位朋友。

sentences.en: Write it as if this person were going to have to read and understand it.
sentences.zh: 写的时候，就当这个人必须阅读并理解它。

sentences.en: Indeed, it is a good idea, if you can, to get just such a person to read your report before handing it in.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果条件允许，最好在提交报告前，就请这样一个人来读一读。

sentences.en: The demands and expectations placed upon you will, of course, vary with your experience of report writing.
sentences.zh: 当然，对你的要求和期望，会随着你撰写报告的经验而变化。

sentences.en: Early on in your study, as an author of experimental reports, less will be expected of you than later.
sentences.zh: 在学习初期，作为实验报告的作者，别人对你的要求会比后期低。

w.m: phr.被要求做到；被寄予期望

sentences.en: At this early stage, you will be expected mainly to show that you understand what you did in your report and its implications, together with evidence that you have, at least, a basic grasp of the demands of the report’s format.
sentences.zh: 在这个早期阶段，你主要需要表明自己理解报告中做了什么及其意义，同时证明自己至少基本掌握了报告格式的要求。

sentences.en: Later on, however, you will be expected to pay more attention to the research significance of what you did.
sentences.zh: 不过，到了后期，你就需要更加关注所做研究的意义。

sentences.en: The “why you did it” part will become more important because, in being responsible for the choice of topic and design, you will be expected to be able to justify this choice.
sentences.zh: “为什么这样做”会变得更重要，因为既然你要对选题和设计负责，就需要能够说明这种选择的合理性。

w.m: v.证明……有道理；为……作出解释

sentences.en: So you must be able to tell us why it is that, given the options available to you, you decided to conduct your particular study.
sentences.zh: 所以，你必须能说明，在现有的各种选择中，为什么决定开展这项研究。

sentences.en: You will need, therefore, to develop the habit of thinking about how the ideas that you are entertaining for your experiment or study will look in the report, paying particular attention to how they will fit into the part of INTRODUCTION.
sentences.zh: 因此，你要养成一种习惯：思考实验或研究中正在考虑的想法，在报告中该如何呈现，尤其要关注它们如何融入“引言”部分。

sentences.en: Specific dangers that you must watch out for here are: first, a lack of adequate material to put in the section.
sentences.zh: 在这里，你尤其要提防以下问题：第一，这一部分缺少充分的材料。

sentences.en: And second, the undertaking of a project that lacks any research justification, because it is based on assumptions that are contradicted by existing findings in the area.
sentences.zh: 第二，所开展的项目缺乏研究上的正当理由，因为其依据的假设，与该领域已有的研究发现相矛盾。

sentences.en: Thinking clearly in advance will help you to avoid making these mistakes.
sentences.zh: 提前想清楚这些问题，会有助于避免犯下这些错误。

sentences.en: OK. Today we’ve had a brief look at the format of an experimental report, what each section is about and some of the basic issues like reader awareness, so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 好，今天我们简要了解了实验报告的格式、各节的内容，以及读者意识等一些基本问题。

sentences.en: Next time, we will discuss how to write up the INTRODUCTION section.
sentences.zh: 下次，我们将讨论如何撰写“引言”部分。
